title: Closed constant coefficient tensors and pullback on the etale site
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with constant ring sheaves $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and ordinary module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] set $P_C=i_*A_C$, with underived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], in degree zero. For every scheme morphism $v:X'\to X$, put $C'=X'\times_XC$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Pullback of locally constant sections on $C\times_XT$, for each etale $T\to X$, defines $P_C\to v_*P_{C'}$. Its adjoint, for the constant-ring inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], is an isomorphism
$$b_{v,C}:v^{-1}P_C\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{C'}.$$
It carries the restriction $A_X\to P_C$ to $A_{X'}\to P_{C'}$. These particular isomorphisms preserve identities and compositions under the canonical composition isomorphism for inverse images.

For closed immersions $C,D\hookrightarrow X$, put $I=C\times_XD$. Restrict locally constant sections on $C\times_XT$ and $D\times_XT$ to $I\times_XT$ and multiply. This gives an isomorphism of sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]
$$\mu_{C,D}:P_C\otimes_{A_X}P_D\xrightarrow{\sim}P_I.$$
Every $P_C$ is flat, meaning that tensoring with it is an exact functor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Consequently the same map on degree-zero flat models gives $\mu_{C,D}:P_C\otimes_A^LP_D\xrightarrow{\sim}P_I$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor] and total tensor as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Under the canonical associators, $\mu_{I,E}(\mu_{C,D}\otimes1)=\mu_{C,D\cap E}(1\otimes\mu_{D,E})$ for every third closed $E$, and $\mu_{D,C}\sigma=\mu_{C,D}$ after the support-interchange identification. For $D'=X'\times_XD$, $I'=X'\times_XI$, the canonical tensor comparison gives
$$b_{v,I}\circ v^{-1}\mu_{C,D}=\mu_{C',D'}\circ(b_{v,C}\otimes b_{v,D}).$$
The same equalities hold for the displayed derived tensors. No finite-type, separatedness, reducedness, or Cartier hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback, especially (3); agent-formulated closed-constant tensor refinement of the stalk calculation, retained from returned item Step 2. Tensor multiplication and flatness are assertions of this lemma, not assertions attributed to Tag 03Q1 alone.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-locally-constant] to identify $A_C(C\times_XT)$ with locally constant $A$-valued functions on $C\times_XT$, naturally in $T$, with pointwise module operations. Thus $P_C(T)$ has exactly this model. Restriction $A_X\to P_C$ is restriction of functions. Precomposition along $C'\times_{X'}(X'\times_XT)\to C\times_XT$ defines an $A_X$-linear map $h_{v,C}:P_C\to v_*P_{C'}$: both its restriction compatibility and its linearity follow from $(a s)\circ q=(a\circ q)(s\circ q)$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] its adjoint $b_{v,C}$ exists and satisfies $v_*b_{v,C}\circ\eta_{v,P_C}=h_{v,C}$. The base-changed supports are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Their intersections are closed immersions into $X$ or $X'$ by that node and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp].

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps; Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback; agent construction of the specified adjoint.

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ whose image belongs to $C$, it factors uniquely through $C$: on an affine chart $C=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$, the map $R\to\Omega$ kills $J$, since $J$ is contained in the point's prime kernel [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Apply [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], using [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying] to forget coefficients. The resulting identification $(P_C)_{\bar x}=A$ sends the germ of a locally constant function to its value at $\bar x$: the first comparison is induced by the neighbourhood base-change functor, and the second sends a constant germ $a$ to $a$. These are $A$-linear, since restrictions and the constant-section maps are $A$-linear. If $\bar x$ is outside $C$, restrict to the open complement $U=X\setminus C$. Every etale $T\to U$ has $C\times_XT=\varnothing$, hence $P_C(T)=0$. Refining any pointed neighbourhood by its inverse image of $U$ shows $(P_C)_{\bar x}=0$ by [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. This argument applies to all the closed supports in step 1.

source.place: Tag 04FX, lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion; Tag 03P5; the outside-support case is the empty-complement argument of 04FX.

proof.text: Fix $\bar x'$ of $X'$ and put $\bar x=v\bar x'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] and the underlying-module compatibility of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], the source stalk of $b_{v,C}$ identifies with $(P_C)_{\bar x}$. Its adjunction equation from step 1 sends a represented germ $s$ to the germ of the pulled-back function $s\circ q$. If $\bar x\in C$, equivalently $\bar x'\in C'$ by the fibre-product universal property, evaluation in step 2 gives $(s\circ q)(\bar x')=s(\bar x)$; the stalk map is $\mathrm{id}_A$. Otherwise both stalks are zero. Thus $b_{v,C}$ is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] on underlying abelian sheaves; its inverse is automatically linear. For $A_X\to P_C$ the same equation gives $a\mapsto a$ on $C'$ and zero outside it. Equivalently, pulling back a function on $T$ and then restricting to $C'$ equals first restricting to $C$ and then pulling back. This proves compatibility with the specified canonical comparison $v^{-1}A_X\cong A_{X'}$ in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (3), including the germ formula; Tag 03PU, theorem-exactness-stalks; agent calculation of the specified map.

proof.text: For $w:X''\to X'$, precomposition of functions gives $h_{v\circ w,C}=v_*h_{w,C'}\circ h_{v,C}$ after the canonical direct-image composition identification. Indeed both sides send $s$ to $s\circ q_v\circ q_w$. The unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], transported to modules using the identical underlying units of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], says that the adjunct of $b_{w,C'}\circ w^{-1}b_{v,C}$ is precisely that composite. Uniqueness of adjuncts therefore identifies it with $b_{v\circ w,C}$ under the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism. For the identity map, $h_{\mathrm{id},C}$ is identity precomposition, and the identity unit equation in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] gives $b_{\mathrm{id},C}=1$ under its canonical comparison. These calculations prove the requested identity and composition laws for these particular maps.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 and direct-image fibre products; canonical composition comparison and its unit equations; agent precomposition calculation.

proof.text: For $I=C\times_XD$, the pairing $(s,t)\mapsto(s|_I)(t|_I)$ is $A_X(T)$-balanced, additive in each variable, and compatible with restriction in $T$. The universal properties of tensor and sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] therefore give the displayed $\mu_{C,D}$. By [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] its stalk sends $s_{\bar x}\otimes t_{\bar x}$ to the product of their values on $I$. This node's tensor over constant scalars agrees with the $A_X$-module tensor here: locally a scalar in $A_X(T)$ is a constant $a\in A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-locally-constant], so after sheafification the $A$-balancing relations already impose all $A_X(T)$-balancing relations, and conversely. At $\bar x\in I$, step 2 identifies the map with $A\otimes_AA\to A$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. If $\bar x\notin I$, at least one source factor and the target are zero. All stalks are isomorphisms, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] gives the claimed sheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 03P5 and 03PU; stalk tensor comparison via the etale point construction; agent product calculation.

proof.text: Apply the existing stalkwise flatness criterion [lem-sfb-etale-flat-geometric-fibers] to P_C. Compare universe-lifted and ordinary stalks by the canonical uliftSheafFiberIso. If the geometric point lies on C, factor its field-valued morphism through the closed immersion, as in [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-open-or-closed]. The closed-direct-image stalk comparison [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar], the universe-lift comparison on C, and the constant-sheaf stalk comparison identify this stalk with A. The free rank-one A-module is flat (ModuleCat.flat_iff_flat and Module.Flat A A). Otherwise the geometric point factors through the open complement of C. The two supports have disjoint ranges, so [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar] makes the inverse image of P_C on that complement zero. Apply the stalk functor, and transport by the inverse-image stalk comparison, to obtain a zero stalk. A zero object is flat. Thus every geometric stalk is flat, and the criterion concludes flatness. This includes the zero ring, empty supports, and empty X.

source.place: Tags 04FX and 03PU; existing source-library stalkwise flatness criterion in WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/UpperLowerStar/FlatModuleCat.lean; identity-or-zero stalk calculation.

proof.text: For three closed supports, evaluate both parenthesized products on section tensors $(s\otimes t)\otimes u$. Restriction to $C\times_XD\times_XE$ gives respectively $(s|_I\,t|_I)|_{I\cap E}\,u|_{I\cap E}$ and $s|_{C\cap(D\cap E)}\,(t|_{D\cap E}\,u|_{D\cap E})$. They agree because iterated restriction is restriction to the triple fibre product and $(ab)c=a(bc)$ in $A$. For interchange, the braiding sends $s\otimes t$ to $t\otimes s$, whose product is unchanged because $ab=ba$. The tensor associator and braiding have exactly these pure-tensor formulas, and a map out of a sheafified tensor is determined on section tensors by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Hence the two sheaf-map equalities hold, with the canonical support identifications. This proves associativity and symmetry of the specific $\mu$ of step 5.

source.place: Agent calculation of pointwise multiplication and tensor universal properties, in the locally constant model of Tag 03P5.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction] to the etale geometric morphism, the constant rings and the module pullback of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Its comparison has the normalization of [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]: on unit images of sections it takes the pullback of $s\otimes t$ to the tensor of the pullbacks of $s$ and $t$. On a stalk $\bar x'$ the inverse-image germ comparison [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] therefore identifies this with the identity comparison of the tensor factors at $v\bar x'$. At points over $I$, the two maps in the asserted square are $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$ by steps 3 and 5; at all other points their source or target is zero. Equality on stalks implies equality of these maps: the image of their difference has zero stalks by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and hence is zero by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. This proves the displayed pullback square for the canonical tensor comparison, including its normalization on the specified $b$ and $\mu$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, normalized pure-tensor construction; also literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, Tags 03Q1 (3) and 03PU.

proof.text: Each $P_C[0]$ is a bounded-above complex of flat sheaves by step 6, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The canonical computation isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] computes its derived tensor with $P_D[0]$ by the total tensor of these very degree-zero complexes. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] this total complex is $(P_C\otimes_{A_X}P_D)[0]$, with zero differential, and the map of step 5 therefore gives the required derived isomorphism. The product is again $P_I[0]$, a flat K-flat model, so the two iterated products can use these same models. The associator is reassociation of the sole degree-zero tensor summand; the symmetry sign is $(-1)^{0\cdot0}=1$. The equalities of step 7 thus remain equal after localization. For pullback, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes the derived inverse image termwise on these complexes; steps 3 and 6 identify their pulled-back terms with flat $P_{C'}$. Its canonical derived tensor comparison on these K-flat models is the localization of the ordinary comparison of step 8, so that square also remains equal after localization. Naturality of the model computation in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] ensures these are the displayed derived maps, rather than new chosen isomorphisms.
